title: Java Doesn't Need a Build Step Anymore
description:
Think Java always means compile-then-run? Since Java 11, you can launch a .java file directly with a single command -- no javac step required. This is lesson 1 of the Java Mastery Path: install the JDK, write your first Hello World, and use the single-file launch shortcut for quick tests.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-1/01-setup/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Everyone thinks Java needs a build step before you can run a single line of code. It doesn't anymore.

display.heading: Java's Hidden Shortcut
display.subheading: Java Mastery Path -- Setup & First Program

beats.narration: Here's the classic Hello World: a public class matching the file name, and a main method the JVM looks for first.
Normally, you compile it into bytecode with javac, then run the class file with java. Two separate steps.
But since Java 11, you can skip all that. Just run java Hello dot java, and it compiles in memory and runs instantly.
No project, no build file, just one line to try Java out. Full setup guide's linked below.
